display.name: Jira
display.blurb: Search, read, create, and transition Jira issues; browse projects and users — authenticated with an Atlassian API token (Basic auth, brokered at the egress proxy).

cli.doc:
Use `jira` to work with Jira Cloud (REST API v3) from this session — search/read issues, create and transition issues, comment, and browse projects/users. Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects the real Atlassian API token (Basic auth) on requests to api.atlassian.com and *.atlassian.net; `JIRA_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder. Do NOT set a real token or run any login.

FIRST set your site. The CLI needs to know which Jira instance to hit (this is NOT a secret):
- Scoped-token gateway (default): `export JIRA_CLOUD_ID=<your-cloud-id>` → requests go to https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<id>/rest/api/3/... . Find your cloud id at https://<site>.atlassian.net/_edgeAuth/jira-cloud-id or via the accessible-resources list.
- Classic site host: `export JIRA_SITE=<your-site>` (the subdomain of <site>.atlassian.net) → requests go to https://<site>.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/... .
Set exactly one; JIRA_CLOUD_ID wins if both are set.

Subcommands:
- `jira whoami` — current user (GET /myself). Needs `myself:read`.
- `jira search '<JQL>' [field=value ...]` — JQL search (GET /search/jql, e.g. `jira search 'project=ENG AND status="In Progress"'`). Needs `issues:read`.
- `jira issue <KEY>` — fetch one issue (GET /issue/KEY). Needs `issues:read`.
- `jira create <PROJECT_KEY> <ISSUETYPE> <summary...>` — create an issue (POST /issue). Needs `issues:write`. Prints the new issue key.
- `jira comment <KEY> <text...>` — add a comment (POST /issue/KEY/comment). Needs `issues:write`.
- `jira transitions <KEY>` — list available transitions (GET /issue/KEY/transitions, needs `issues:read`); `jira transition <KEY> <transition-id>` performs one (POST, needs `issues:write`).
- `jira projects` — list projects (GET /project/search). Needs `projects:read`.
- `jira users [field=value ...]` — search users (GET /user/search). Needs `users:read`.
- `jira get <path> [field=value ...]` / `jira post <path> [json]` — raw call against /rest/api/3/<path> (e.g. `jira get issue/ENG-1`). Needs the matching read/write power for that path.

Responses are JSON. Errors come back as {"errorMessages":[...],"errors":{...}}. A path your profile didn't grant is denied at the network boundary, not authenticated.
